description: Believes a parameterized query still returns all rows for an injection payload, not realizing bound values are treated as data and never parsed as SQL.
Believes SQL injection payloads usually just break the query with a syntax error, rather than being crafted to keep the statement valid (balanced quotes, comments).
Believes text after a SQL -- comment still takes effect, so injected comments cannot remove password or status filters.
Believes placeholders can bind table or column identifiers, when parameters only bind values and identifiers need allow-listing.
Believes all database drivers use the same placeholder syntax (?, %s, $1, :1) rather than driver-specific paramstyles.
Believes a character-class allow-list regex or an integer check on a transformed value is enough, ignoring that checks like Number() coercion or unanchored patterns may admit payloads.
Believes blocking a few bad strings (';', '&&', '127.0.0.1', 'localhost') is enough, overlooking alternatives like '|', '$()', or decimal IP encodings.
Believes string-built commands with shell=True or os.system are safe for user input, instead of passing an argv list with shell=False.
Believes shlex.quote does not neutralize shell metacharacters, or that shlex.split stops at operators like semicolons.
Believes ';' is the only command-chaining metacharacter, forgetting &&, ||, |, backticks, and $() substitution.
Believes metacharacters in an argument still start a second command when run with an argv list and shell=False.
Believes os.path.normpath or abspath leave '..' segments in place or are no use for resolving traversal, rather than collapsing them lexically.
Believes os.path.join(base, user_path) always stays under base, ignoring that an absolute second argument discards the base.
Believes path.startswith(base) proves containment, ignoring sibling directories like /var/www-secret and unresolved '..' or symlinks.
Believes encoded sequences like %2e%2e%2f or %5c are harmless, forgetting they decode into '../' or '..\' traversal.
Believes os.path.basename keeps directory parts or is not an effective way to strip traversal components from a filename.
Believes the text before '@' in a URL is the host, when it is userinfo and the real host is after the '@'.
Believes startswith, substring or suffix-like checks on a URL host are safe, ignoring lookalikes such as api.example.com.evil.net.
Believes blocking 127.0.0.1 and localhost covers internal addresses, ignoring link-local metadata IPs, 0.0.0.0, IPv6 ::1 and decimal/octal encodings.
Believes URL scheme validation is unnecessary because only http(s) is ever fetched, overlooking file:// and other schemes.
Believes hashing the same password with different salts yields the same digest, missing the point of per-user salts.
Believes == is the right way to compare tokens, MACs or hashes, rather than constant-time comparison like hmac.compare_digest.
Believes base64 (e.g. in Basic auth headers or JWT segments) hides or protects data, when it is a keyless reversible encoding.
Believes the JWT payload is secret because it looks opaque, when anyone can base64url-decode its claims without the key.
Believes a minimum length plus one digit rule makes passwords strong, rather than storing them with a slow salted hash and checking breached lists.
Believes fast general hashes like MD5 or SHA-256 are suitable for password storage, instead of a slow adaptive hash such as bcrypt or argon2.
Believes a token is valid when exp is less than now, or misreads the direction of expiry comparisons.
Believes keeping the same session ID across login is fine, not seeing that it enables session fixation and that the ID must be regenerated.
Believes HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite are interchangeable cookie flags, or that SameSite=None works without Secure.
Believes secrets.token_hex(n) returns n characters, rather than 2n hex characters for n random bytes.
Believes it is fine to take roles or admin flags from request query or body parameters instead of the server-side authenticated identity.
Believes being authenticated is enough to access a resource by ID, skipping per-object ownership checks that prevent IDOR.
Believes unknown roles or actions are allowed by default, rather than designing authorization as deny-by-default with explicit grants.
Believes pickle.loads is a safe deserializer like json.loads, when it can invoke arbitrary callables via __reduce__ on untrusted data.
Believes JSON parsers accept trailing commas or single quotes, and that duplicate keys are resolved the same way by every parser.
Believes recursively merging user JSON into objects is safe, missing that a __proto__ key can pollute Object.prototype and affect all objects.
Believes type or truthiness checks on input are reliable, forgetting that bool is an int in Python, "0" and "false" are truthy strings in JS, and whitespace-padded values slip through.
Believes a simple email regex or LIKE pattern proves an address is valid and deliverable, accepting things like user@localhost or ignoring length and byte-size limits.
